question: Which of the following is the most common nutritional cause of anaemia?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron deficiency**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iron deficiency** is the most common nutritional cause of anaemia.
 
• Anaemia is a condition characterized by a lack of healthy red blood cells or hemoglobin, which are crucial for carrying oxygen to the body's tissues.
 
• Iron is a vital component of hemoglobin, and its deficiency leads to reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood.
 
• Common symptoms of iron deficiency anaemia include fatigue, weakness, pale skin, and shortness of breath.
 
• Dietary sources of iron include red meat, poultry, fish, lentils, beans, and iron-fortified cereals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Anaemia** can also be caused by other factors such as vitamin B12 deficiency, folate deficiency, chronic diseases, and genetic disorders.
 
• Regular screening and blood tests can help in early detection and management of anaemia.
 
• Iron supplements and dietary modifications are common treatments for iron deficiency anaemia.
 
• In severe cases, medical interventions such as intravenous iron therapy or blood transfusions may be necessary.
